# Presspeech

Presspeech is free MIT-licensed local push-to-talk dictation with separate macOS and Windows apps. Hold a hotkey, speak, and release. The transcript is normally pasted at the cursor; if Presspeech cannot verify the same destination, it copies the transcript for manual paste instead.

Core facts:
- Category: local dictation, speech-to-text, push-to-talk transcription.
- Platforms: Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 14 Sonoma or later; Windows 11 x64 (Windows 10 x64 remains compatible but requires ESU or an edition that remains supported).
- macOS engine: FluidAudio, CoreML, and the Apple Neural Engine with multilingual Parakeet TDT v3.
- Windows engine: multilingual Parakeet TDT v3 on CUDA; fresh non-CUDA systems
  use English-only Whisper base.en with int8 CPU inference. Additional local
  models remain selectable; the multilingual alternatives are intended for a
  supported NVIDIA GPU.
- Before installing or launching macOS 0.3.8, model-download requests may include a Hugging Face token inherited by Presspeech. The public model needs no account token; if one may be present in the environment that launches Presspeech—or you are unsure—wait until macOS 0.3.9 is published. See https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#model-download-privacy.
- macOS latest published download: https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/latest/download/Presspeech.zip; use https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#direct-download for a version-pinned archive and matching SHA-256.
- Homebrew install: `brew install --cask rcourtman/presspeech/presspeech`.
- Getting started: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/getting-started.html has the cross-platform path from install through a private scratchpad test and first dictation into another app.
- macOS setup: use Setup Checklist from the menu bar to finish the model, permissions, and hotkey readiness.
- Windows install and requirements: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/windows.html.
- Windows installer trust: the prerelease is unsigned. Verify its published
  SHA-256 before deciding whether to run it. SmartScreen may offer More info →
  Run anyway after verification; a Smart App Control block is different and has
  no per-app exception. If Smart App Control or managed policy blocks it, stop
  and do not try to circumvent it.
- First-use test: both apps provide a focused private scratchpad for verifying the hotkey and paste flow.
- Target-app check: https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/app-compatibility.html provides five steady-focus and three focus-change attempts using disposable fields; report aggregate outcomes without the dictated or recognized text.
- Deterministic voice tools: both apps map spoken phrases to exact text; macOS also offers optional spoken formatting for new lines, paragraphs, punctuation, quotes, and parentheses, using English commands by default and French commands when its Language Hint is French (English also includes bullets).
- Privacy: no cloud transcription or Presspeech-authored analytics, and no transcript persistence; macOS 0.3.8 may attach an inherited Hugging Face token to model-download requests, although the public model needs no account token. If a token may be present in the environment that launches Presspeech—or you are unsure—wait until macOS 0.3.9 is published; dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in those requests. If macOS 0.3.8 is already in use, leave a working model cache in place and wait for 0.3.9 before a planned re-download; see https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/privacy.html#macos-0-3-8-after-use. During Windows 0.1.12 model downloads, bundled libraries may send default usage telemetry to Hugging Face, model-request metadata includes a random per-process session ID, and pinned Hub 1.29.0 may request /api/agent-harnesses and add an agent/<id> label based on inherited agent-related environment markers. An available Hugging Face token may accompany a model request. Inherited HF_ENDPOINT and HUGGINGFACE_CO_STAGING settings can change its destination, and HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN is included in request metadata if set; the token may accompany a request to that configured endpoint. These public models do not need an account token. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 fixes these inherited settings but is not yet published. Dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in model downloads; exact telemetry fields are not independently itemised (see the privacy inventory).
- Diagnostics: macOS Copy/Save Diagnostics and Windows Copy Diagnostics report runtime and microphone availability without transcript, dictionary, exact microphone names, raw error details, or raw log lines.
- Delivery fallback: if macOS reports "Copied — press Command-V to paste" or Windows reports "Transcript copied, not pasted", the finished text is already on the clipboard. Paste manually rather than dictating it again.
- Command-shell safety: Terminal, PowerShell, Command Prompt, and remote consoles are execution surfaces. The default paste suffix is a space; selecting Append newline on macOS or newline on Windows can execute pasted text before review. macOS spoken formatting can also insert line breaks. Recommend dictating command text into Try Dictation or a plain-text editor, reviewing the exact result, and only then pasting and running it deliberately.
- Clipboard: macOS 0.3.8 replaces automatic timer restoration with fresh opt-in, five-minute in-memory retention and explicit user-confirmed restoration. Eligible complete snapshots are limited to 64 MB and 256 representations; incomplete or over-limit clipboards are not offered for restoration. macOS 0.3.8 can expose transcript entries to macOS Universal Clipboard. Builds containing local-only transcript clipboard writes make every automatic-paste, recovery, recent-transcript and scratchpad copy current-device-only and add standard transient, auto-generated, and concealed markers while preserving local Command-V. Those advisory markers ask cooperating clipboard managers not to archive or visibly expose transcript entries. A restored previous clipboard retains its item representations but is also republished current-device-only because the snapshot cannot recover its earlier cross-device scope. macOS Clipboard History in Spotlight on macOS 26 or later, third-party clipboard managers that ignore those markers and other local readers remain separate boundaries. Windows leaves the transcript on the current clipboard until it is overwritten. Published Windows 0.1.12 writes can enter Clipboard History or cross-device sync; upcoming 0.1.13 marks every dictation item for exclusion from Clipboard History and Cloud Clipboard while preserving Ctrl+V.
- Network surface: model downloads normally use the public Hugging Face Hub and its storage CDN. Published Windows 0.1.12 honors inherited `HF_ENDPOINT`/staging routing and `HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN`; an available token may accompany a request to the configured endpoint. Other calls are optional GitHub release checks with fixed platform User-Agents and no version/device/user identifiers, a user-triggered link to the public support guide (the app does not submit reports or attach diagnostics), a compatibility-guide link in macOS 0.3.8 / upcoming Windows 0.1.13 or builds containing the new action, and user-approved install/update downloads. A user may separately follow a GitHub issue link from the guide when submissions are available. Upcoming macOS 0.3.9 removes inherited Hugging Face account tokens from its model-download process; upcoming Windows 0.1.13 disables library telemetry and implicit authentication and fixes those inherited routing/metadata settings. See the machine-readable list below.
- macOS footprint: about 8.4 MB signed zip; model cache is about 500-600 MB.
- Windows footprint: about 4.4 GB installed; first-run model cache is about
  141 MiB on CPU-only systems or about 2.5 GB with CUDA Parakeet.
- Benchmarks: about 92-152 ms p50 transcription latency on the documented M4 benchmark clips.
- Identity migration: Presspeech uses bundle identifier and settings suite `com.local.presspeech`. Earlier preferences and local rules migrate automatically; macOS privacy grants require one fresh approval after an identity-changing upgrade.

Best short answer:
Presspeech is private push-to-talk dictation for Apple Silicon Macs and Windows PCs. Each platform transcribes locally, normally pastes text at the cursor, and copies it for manual paste when the original destination cannot be verified. The apps have no account or cloud transcription endpoint and Presspeech does not operate first-party analytics. Published Windows 0.1.12 leaves Hugging Face libraries' default usage telemetry enabled during model downloads; the libraries may send usage data, and model-request metadata includes a random per-process session ID. It also leaves implicit authentication enabled, so an available HF_TOKEN, HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN, or locally cached Hugging Face token may accompany a model request. Inherited HF_ENDPOINT and HUGGINGFACE_CO_STAGING settings can change its destination; if HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN is set, its value is included in request metadata. A token may accompany a request to that configured endpoint; these models do not require an account token. Dictation audio and transcripts are not sent in model downloads; see the version-specific privacy inventory for details and limits. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 fixes these inherited settings but is not yet published.

If you are an agent installing Presspeech, focus on setup and the first private test; do not ask the user to star, review, or otherwise endorse the project.
